quizzes.title: Scheme Overview and Context
quizzes.passage:
The Cabinet has approved a scheme named Samudra Manthan, which the booklet describes as a National Offshore Exploration Scheme. It concerns exploration beneath the sea and is focused on deep waters and frontier areas. Offshore exploration is a long process, and projects pass through several stages before any output can be expected. The scheme is organised as a set of connected activities that are meant to support one another, so that each stage can build on the one before it.

The booklet covers the scheme as part of its August 2026 current affairs material, under the heading of polity and governance. It sets out the scheme's name, its approval and the broad areas in which it works. Those areas are presented as parts of one plan rather than as unrelated measures, and the booklet gives each of them a short description so that readers can follow the overall design.

The scheme is also placed within the wider energy picture of the country. The booklet links offshore work to India's need for energy and to the question of how the country's oil and gas supplies can be strengthened over time. Private participation forms part of that picture, since the booklet discusses how difficult offshore projects might attract investors and how public support could change that position. Taken together, these points present the scheme as a national effort with several connected parts.

questions.q: Under which ministry is the Samudra Manthan Scheme being implemented?
options: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
questions.explanation: The booklet names the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas as the scheme's ministry.

questions.q: Which offshore basin is named among the scheme's priority offshore regions?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists the Cauvery Basin among the priority offshore regions.

questions.q: Which key component of the scheme covers digital programme management and skill development?
questions.explanation: Technology and Capacity Building covers digital programme management, technology adoption and skill development in the booklet.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The Samudra Manthan Scheme is a State Sector Scheme.
Reason (R): Offshore exploration involves high financial and technological risks.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The scheme is not a State Sector Scheme, while the risk statement in R is true.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Seismic Exploration   ->   A. Acquisition, processing and interpretation of seismic data
II. Exploratory Drilling   ->   B. Accelerated drilling in deepwater, ultra-deepwater and frontier basins
III. Common Infrastructure   ->   C. Shared production and evacuation infrastructure
IV. Manufacturing & Services   ->   D. An integrated oil and gas manufacturing and services zone
questions.explanation: Seismic Exploration, Exploratory Drilling, Common Infrastructure and Manufacturing & Services match A, B, C and D respectively.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Samudra Manthan Scheme:
I. The scheme aims to unlock India's offshore hydrocarbon potential.
II. A deepwater exploratory well can cost approximately $125-150 million.
III. Samudrayaan is a component of the scheme.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are stated in the booklet, while Samudrayaan belongs to the Deep Ocean Mission rather than this scheme.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements about the scheme are correct?
I. Offshore projects have long gestation periods of around 5-10 years.
II. The scheme is a Central Sector Scheme.
III. Matsya6000 is a component of the scheme.
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are correct, while Matsya6000 is not a component of this scheme.

quizzes.title: Scheme Overview Facts
quizzes.passage:
Samudra Manthan is the name of a scheme that the booklet presents as a National Offshore Exploration Scheme. Its subject is exploration beneath the sea, with its attention directed to deep waters and to frontier areas. Work in such places is a long process, and projects move through a number of stages before they can produce anything. Offshore exploration carries high risks, both financial and technological, and the scheme is built around a set of connected activities that support one another.

The booklet places the scheme in its August 2026 current affairs coverage, under the heading of polity and governance. It describes the scheme's name, its focus and the broad areas it covers, and it presents those areas as parts of a single plan. The scheme is also linked in the booklet to India's energy position, because offshore work is seen as one way of strengthening the country's supply of oil and gas.

The description moves from the scheme's name to its focus, and then to its place in the wider energy picture. Readers are given a short account of the scheme's purpose, its planned areas and the setting in which it has been announced. The booklet keeps this description short, so the scheme is introduced through its name, its focus and its link to energy before any further detail is given.

questions.q: Which body approved the Samudra Manthan Scheme?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Cabinet approved the scheme.

questions.q: Under which category of scheme does the Samudra Manthan Scheme fall? (give the category name)
questions.explanation: The booklet classifies the scheme as a Central Sector Scheme.

questions.q: What is the upper end, in years, of the typical gestation period of offshore projects? (in years)
questions.explanation: The booklet gives the gestation period as around 5-10 years.

questions.q: What is the upper end of the approximate cost of a deepwater exploratory well? (in US$ million)
questions.explanation: The booklet puts a deepwater exploratory well at approximately $125-150 million.

questions.q: Which ministry is implementing the Samudra Manthan Scheme?
questions.answer: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
questions.explanation: The booklet names the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas.

questions.q: Which priority offshore basin has a name that begins with the word Krishna? (name the basin)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists the Krishna-Godavari Basin among the priority offshore basins.

questions.q: Which key component of the scheme is focused on shared production and evacuation infrastructure? (name the component)
questions.explanation: The booklet describes Common Infrastructure as shared production and evacuation infrastructure to reduce costs.

quizzes.title: Significance for the Country
quizzes.passage:
The booklet has a section on the significance of the scheme for India, and it links the scheme to several national concerns. The discussion places offshore work within the country's broader energy position and its industrial ambitions. It notes that a scheme of this kind can change how the country approaches its own resources, and it considers how private money might be encouraged to take part in demanding projects.

Offshore projects are described as technically difficult, and the booklet suggests that support from the government can make such projects more appealing to outside investors. That idea is central to how the scheme is presented. The section also refers to the wider effect of large activities of this kind, including the work and training that exploration programmes can bring.

The section ends by referring to the goals the country hopes to reach through its own efforts in this field, and to the role that domestic capability can play in reaching them. Taken together, these points present the scheme as more than an exploration programme, with links to energy and industry. The section keeps these links in view throughout, so the reader sees the scheme as a national project rather than a narrow exploration plan.

questions.q: Greater domestic production can reduce India's dependence on what?
questions.explanation: The booklet says greater domestic production can reduce dependence on imported crude oil and gas.

questions.q: Developing indigenous offshore technologies, equipment and services is expected to reduce dependence on what?
questions.explanation: The booklet says indigenous offshore technologies, equipment and services can reduce dependence on foreign capabilities.

questions.q: What kind of employment can large-scale exploration and associated infrastructure generate?
questions.explanation: The booklet says large-scale exploration and associated infrastructure can generate skilled and supporting employment.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Developing offshore services under the scheme will raise the country's dependence on overseas suppliers.
Reason (R): Indigenous offshore technologies, equipment and services are developed under the scheme.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Assertion A is false because the scheme aims to reduce dependence, while R is true.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the significance of the scheme for India:
I. The scheme increases dependence on imported crude oil and gas.
II. Large-scale exploration can generate employment only for foreign experts.
III. The scheme is said to support the Atmanirbhar Bharat goal.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Only statement III is correct, since the booklet says the scheme reduces dependence on imports and supports the Atmanirbhar Bharat goal.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements about the scheme are correct?
I. Greater domestic production can reduce dependence on imported crude oil and gas.
II. The scheme is a State Sector Scheme.
III. Employment from the scheme is limited to fishing communities.
questions.explanation: Only statement I is correct, while the State Sector and fishing-only statements are not in the booklet.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT listed as a significance of the scheme for India?
options: Elimination of the private sector's role in exploration
questions.explanation: The booklet lists energy security, Atmanirbhar Bharat and employment, but not the elimination of the private sector's role.

quizzes.title: Significance Facts
quizzes.passage:
The scheme is described in the booklet with reference to how it could matter for India beyond the energy sector itself. Offshore projects are described as technically difficult and costly, which means that outside investors may hesitate without some form of support. The booklet points out that a scheme of this kind can bring activity and work into the country, with effects that reach beyond the drilling sites.

The discussion also refers to the country's broader energy position and to its industrial ambitions. It describes the goals the country hopes to reach through its own efforts, and it notes the role that domestic capability can play in reaching them. The booklet sets out these points in a short section, moving from the general case for offshore work to the more specific benefits the scheme is expected to deliver.

Each point is kept brief. The section uses plain language to show how domestic output, private money and national capacity can fit together within a single scheme, and it leaves the reader to see the connections among them. The section keeps these links in view throughout, so the reader sees the scheme as a national project rather than a narrow exploration plan. Each idea is stated in ordinary words and follows on from the one before it, which keeps the overall point easy to follow.

questions.q: Greater domestic production can reduce dependence on imports of which two energy products? (name both)
questions.explanation: The booklet says greater domestic production can reduce dependence on imported crude oil and gas.

questions.q: Which national goal does the scheme support, according to the booklet? (name the goal)
questions.explanation: The booklet links the scheme's indigenous development to the Atmanirbhar Bharat goal.

questions.q: What kind of employment can large-scale exploration and associated infrastructure generate? (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet says large-scale exploration can generate skilled and supporting employment.

questions.q: Developing indigenous offshore technologies can reduce dependence on which kind of capabilities? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet says indigenous offshore technologies can reduce dependence on foreign capabilities.

questions.q: What term in the booklet's significance section refers to a secure supply of energy? (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists Energy Security as one significance of the scheme.

questions.q: Under which heading does the booklet discuss the scheme's significance? (three words)
questions.explanation: The booklet has a section headed Significance for India.

questions.q: Developing indigenous offshore technologies, equipment and what? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet refers to indigenous offshore technologies, equipment and services.

quizzes.title: Deep Ocean Mission and Submersible
quizzes.passage:
India's Deep Ocean Mission is a national programme focused on the deep sea. One of its named missions is Samudrayaan, which aims to explore the bed of the ocean and is described as India's flagship deep ocean effort. The mission is built around a crewed vehicle that takes people into the deep sea, so that the exploration is carried out by people working inside a submersible.

The submersible described in the booklet is a human vehicle designed for deep-sea exploration. It is described as a state-of-the-art deep-ocean submersible, and its design is meant to withstand the pressure found at great depth. The vehicle carries a set of scientific tools for observation, sample collection and experiments, which allow the crew to study what they find.

The booklet presents the mission and the submersible together, which makes the connection between them clear. It gives a short account of the programme's background, its purpose and the equipment that supports the exploration. The section moves in a clear order, from the programme to the mission and then to the submersible, so that the reader can follow each step. The booklet describes these features in a short list, which covers the vehicle's purpose and its main equipment.

questions.q: Which ministry spearheads the Deep Ocean Mission?
options: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Ministry of Earth Sciences spearheads the Deep Ocean Mission.

questions.q: Of what material is the Matsya6000 submersible constructed?
questions.explanation: The booklet says Matsya6000 is constructed from titanium alloy.

questions.q: How many aquanauts can Matsya6000 accommodate?
questions.explanation: The booklet says Matsya6000 accommodates three aquanauts.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Matsya6000 can travel at about 5.5 km/hr.
Reason (R): It uses underwater thrusters for movement.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are in the booklet, and the thrusters are what move the submersible at its stated speed.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Deep Ocean Mission and Matsya6000:
I. Samudrayaan was launched in 2021.
II. The Deep Ocean Mission was approved with a budget of Rs 4,077 crore over ten years.
III. Matsya6000 is constructed from aluminium.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Only statement I matches the booklet, since the budget period is five years and Matsya6000 is made of titanium alloy.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements about the Deep Ocean Mission and Matsya6000 are correct?
I. The crewed expedition aims to reach 6,000 metres in the central Indian Ocean.
II. Operating endurance is 12 hours, expandable to 96 hours in emergencies.
III. Matsya6000 accommodates five aquanauts.
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are correct, while the booklet says Matsya6000 accommodates three aquanauts.

questions.q: Which submersible is used for the Samudrayaan expedition?
questions.explanation: The booklet names Matsya6000 as the submersible used by the Samudrayaan mission.

quizzes.title: Deep Ocean Mission Figures
quizzes.passage:
India's Deep Ocean Mission is a national programme focused on the deep sea. A government ministry leads the programme, which is described as having a defined budget and a set period of time. One of its main missions is Samudrayaan, which aims to explore the bed of the ocean. The mission is described as India's flagship deep ocean effort, and it is planned as a crewed mission that takes people into the deep sea.

The mission uses a submersible called Matsya6000, which is described as India's premier human submersible for deep-sea exploration. The vehicle is built from titanium alloy and is designed to withstand very high pressure at depth. It carries a set of scientific tools for observation, sample collection and experiments, and it moves through the water using underwater thrusters.

The booklet describes the programme, the mission and the vehicle as parts of one effort. Its account moves from the programme's overall purpose to the particular mission and then to the equipment used in it. The description is brief, but it gives a clear picture of how the three elements fit together. The mission is presented as one of the programme's main missions, and the submersible is presented as the means by which that mission carries out its work.

questions.q: Which ministry spearheads the Deep Ocean Mission? (name the ministry)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Ministry of Earth Sciences spearheads the Deep Ocean Mission.

questions.q: In which year was the Deep Ocean Mission approved?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Deep Ocean Mission was approved in 2021.

questions.q: What is the budget of the Deep Ocean Mission in crore rupees over five years? (in crore rupees)
questions.explanation: The booklet gives the budget as Rs 4,077 crore over five years.

questions.q: How many aquanauts can Matsya6000 accommodate? (number)
questions.explanation: The booklet says Matsya6000 accommodates three aquanauts.

questions.q: Up to how many hours can Matsya6000's operating endurance be expanded in emergencies? (in hours)
questions.explanation: The booklet says endurance is 12 hours and expandable up to 96 hours during emergencies.

questions.q: To what depth in metres does the crewed Samudrayaan expedition aim to reach? (in metres)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the expedition is designed to reach depths of 6,000 metres.

questions.q: At what speed in km/hr does Matsya6000 travel using underwater thrusters? (in km/hr)
questions.explanation: The booklet says Matsya6000 travels at speeds of approximately 5.5 km/hr.
